defects: MAJOR desktop.py:654-665 together with hotkeys.py:375-399. The ask hold-to-talk session stops by itself about 1.2 s after it starts while the user is still holding the combo. _begin_ask injects MARKER key-ups for every held combo modifier (D1). Those key-ups update GetAsyncKeyState, so the modifier now reads as released. A held modifier does not auto-repeat once another key was pressed later (Windows repeats only the last key). After PHYSICAL_CHECK_SECONDS (1.2 s), _sync_physical therefore treats the modifier as physically released, synthesizes its key-up and emits ('stop', None), because the hold was longer than hold_seconds. Measured with the real App: LeftAlt+VK0x86 held 3 s -> recording 0.23 s .. 1.25 s, ptt.recovered ['0xa4']. LeftAlt+LeftCtrl (modifier-only analogue of the new default RightAlt+RightCtrl) -> recording 0.24 s .. 1.27 s. Dictate with LeftAlt+VK0x87 held 3 s does not stop (no release), so the stop is specific to ask. T20's own spec requires 'state machine still sees the key held'. With the new default on a machine without Typeless, both RightCtrl and RightAlt are released this way, so the default 隨便問 hold-to-talk truncates the spoken question to about 1 s. T17 already did this for LeftAlt; T20 extends it to every combo modifier, including the default. check_wave_d holds only 0.3 s (check_wave_d.py:204), so it cannot detect this. Fix direction: tell PushToTalk which vks were released by injection (for example, mark them never-seen-physically or exempt them from _sync_physical until their real key-up), and add a >= 2 s hold check.

MINOR hotkeys.py:177,281-291 vs 375-399. A key that the hook itself swallowed never updates GetAsyncKeyState (measured: async Space false while swallowed, true when bare). The physical-state recovery therefore can never repair a lost key-up of a swallowed key, for example after a hook timeout. Simulated: Space stays in held_keys indefinitely, the next LeftAlt-alone press starts 'ask', and the next bare Space press is swallowed once. Before T20 the same Space would have been recoverable. Narrow (needs a missed key-up), but it is a new failure mode of the swallow rule.

NIT desktop.py:664-666. When capture_selection then skips (non_text/busy), _begin_ask has already injected the NOOP pair and MARKER key-ups for held modifiers. capture_selection itself injects nothing (verified), and these events are harmless releases, but 'capture skipped -> no key injected' holds only at the context.py level.

NIT hotkeys.py:85-94 + desktop.py:521. Migration has no version marker: a user who deliberately sets RightAlt+Space as the only ask combo has it silently replaced on every launch. The spec accepts this behaviour; a warning in the hotkey UI would make it visible.

NIT audiofocus.py:10. The docstring says 'the user manual cites this', but USER_MANUAL.md has no mute / Volume Mixer text (and no 隨便問 section at all). Docs were out of T20 scope; the planner should schedule the manual update.
T20.notes: All five listed acceptance commands pass when re-run, and every original defect (D1-D3, m1-m8) is fixed at the cited lines. Independent real-machine reproductions (a), (b) capture part and (c) pass. FAIL comes from the new adversarial finding N1: a hold-to-talk 隨便問 session is cut off about 1.2 s after start because the D1 release makes the physical-state recovery drop the released modifier. That violates T20's own requirement that the state machine still sees the key held, and it breaks the default combo's primary interaction (press and hold to speak). Observation, not a defect (the spec mandates it): capture is now skipped whenever the clipboard holds any format other than text/locale. Text copied from browsers, Word or VS Code carries such formats (HTML/RTF/editor data), so in practice the selection capture may often be skipped with the SKIP_MESSAGES status.
